Nariway Daily Check-in

15 August 2026

Needs your attention / action today

Weekend prep for Monday's Qwoted launch. Query A is set to post Monday morning, Aug 17 — not Friday, since PR/source activity runs Mon–Thu. Five things need to happen before then:

  • Get nariway.com live with the Fisher fix and locked advisory wording — the live site still shows the old copy, this is the real blocker.
  • Lock Query A as the first query, with a ~1-week response window.
  • Post the first Substack Note from the queue, so a respondent who checks Artobiography sees an active publication, not one dormant since Jan 2025.
  • Ready the interview kit (question sets, pitch reply, credibility test).
  • Line up 2–3 warm/direct targets (Diana Wierbicki, Matthew F. Erskine, a foundation founder) for parallel outreach next week.

QA critical, one-line fix. cases/neue-galerie.md has verification: verified, which isn't a valid value and overstates the case — report-dataset.md codes this same case Spot-verified, with a source flagged for re-fetch. Fix: change the frontmatter to verification: spot-verified.

A settled decision still reads open. company/decisions/2026-08-12-email-delivery.md still says "Status, awaiting Alina," but Resend has been confirmed live for the daily emails since Aug 14. Worth a one-line status update so it stops looking like an open decision.

Still pending from Thursday, unconfirmed a second day: the hygiene sweep's inferred priority: high on fisher-sfmoma — say yes or correct it.

Nothing else is due or overdue. No partner follow-up is due (Judith Prowda and Rebecca Fine are both set for Aug 26), no other decision is waiting on you, and no exhibition or preview enters the 3-week window (the Medaugh Hiroshige preview, Sept 11, is already on your calendar).

Work log: yesterday's hours (Aug 14, ~7h estimated) are logged as a draft — reply to confirm or correct.

Today I learned

A foundation's governance can be locked in over a decade before the museum even exists. Ernst Beyeler chartered Fondation Beyeler in 1982 — fifteen years before the museum opened and twenty-eight years before his 2010 death — the earliest, most complete pre-death governance lock-in the case dataset has found so far. It handed control to a fully independent board with no family option available at all (he had no children), and sixteen years on it is thriving and actively expanding. It's the sharpest evidence yet for the report's central claim: governance, not family continuity or endowment size, is what decides whether a great collection outlives its founder. → source note

What changed, and what it means

  • Case dataset moved from 36 to 44 of 50, and corporate collections now split into three distinct fates instead of one blurry "corporate collections are fragile" story: forced liquidation on parent bankruptcy (Lehman, Enron), voluntary retreat while the parent stays healthy (Deutsche Bank closing PalaisPopulaire), and unaffected continuity through four mergers over 65 years (JPMorgan Chase). That's a sharper, more publishable framework for the flagship report.
  • The Vogel Collection case is the sample's first zero-endowment durability test. Herbert and Dorothy Vogel funded their entire collecting life on a postal clerk's and a librarian's salary, then pre-executed a 50-states distribution years before either died — and it reads as more durable, by construction, than several cases with nine-figure endowments and a single point of governance failure.
  • Fisher/SFMOMA number resolved: the loan is 720+ works across 100 artists (SFMOMA the primary lender), not the earlier 1,000+ figure, and homepage copy is now locked — this was the actual blocker on getting nariway.com live for Monday.
  • Board-membership decided (qualified yes, right board only), and a whole-field search — not just the BoardAssist database — filed a 10-candidate shortlist to board-opportunities.md, ranked by fit and give/get. Nothing to act on yet; worth a look when there's bandwidth.
  • CFO flag: two straight days of enrichment (case coding, board research, a QA audit) with no client-facing activity since the Dawn call. Monday's Qwoted post is the first scheduled market-facing test since then — the weekend prep above is what actually converts enrichment back into outreach.

Where we stand

The case for the thesis keeps getting sharper on paper (44 of 50 now coded, with a real analytical framework emerging on how corporate collections specifically fail or survive), but the one question that decides everything — whether anyone will pay — still has no new evidence. What's different today is that there's now a date on the calendar for the first real test of it: Monday's Qwoted Query A post, if the weekend prep lands.
